prompt:
Build a nonlinear single-engine fighter-aircraft simulation with twelve-state six-degree-of-freedom rigid-body dynamics. Use a north-east-down inertial frame, report altitude as minus inertial down position, and use standard body axes x forward, y right, z down. Attitude is the 3-2-1 yaw-pitch-roll orientation from body to inertial coordinates; p, q, and r are body angular rates, not Euler-angle derivatives. The minimum topology is a finite-mass/inertia rigid body; altitude-dependent atmosphere; relative-wind air-data calculation; nonlinear aerodynamic force and moment dependence on angle of attack, sideslip, body rates and actual control surfaces; gravity and thrust; five finite-response actuators; and a feedback controller. Directly prescribing the aircraft state or replaying a trajectory is not valid.

Read altitude_reference, airspeed_reference, heading_change, initial_altitude_offset, initial_airspeed_offset, command_time, gust_speed, gust_heading, and gust_time from base-workspace variables. Nominal values are 3048 m, 150 m/s, 0.30 rad, -120 m, -10 m/s, 4.0 s, 12 m/s, 90 deg, and 9.0 s. Their operating ranges are respectively 1900--9000 m, 125--230 m/s, -0.65--0.65 rad, -350--350 m, -30--30 m/s, 3--7 s, 0--25 m/s, -180--180 deg, and 6--13 s. These ranges make every allowed initial altitude 1550--9350 m and every allowed initial airspeed 95--260 m/s. Initialize near a physically plausible steady-flight condition at the requested initial altitude and airspeed. Apply heading_change at command_time. gust_heading is clockwise from north and defines an actual horizontal air-mass velocity in the north-east-down frame. Apply that velocity for 1.5 s beginning at gust_time. Compute relative air velocity as ground velocity minus this gust vector before transforming it into body axes; air_data must log this same applied NED vector. The gust must enter the relative-wind aerodynamics rather than only a log.

Use mass 9295.438666 kg, reference area 27.870912 m^2, span 9.144 m, mean aerodynamic chord 3.450336 m, and inertia matrix [12874.844646 0 1331.412957; 0 75673.607738 0; 1331.412957 0 85552.095321] kg*m^2. The nonlinear aerodynamic representation may use tables or smooth coefficient surfaces; its internal coordinates and control design are not prescribed, but forces and moments must vary causally with dynamic pressure, angle of attack, sideslip, rates and actual surface deflections.

Bound thrust to 4448.22--84516.18 N, elevator to +/-0.436332313 rad, aileron to +/-0.375245789 rad, rudder to +/-0.523598776 rad, and leading-edge flap to 0--0.436332313 rad. Limit their rates respectively to 44482.2 N/s, 1.047197551 rad/s, 1.396263402 rad/s, 2.094395102 rad/s, and 0.436332313 rad/s. Across the declared range, regulate altitude, true airspeed and heading, keep sideslip controlled, remain inside angle-of-attack -0.34906585--0.785398163 rad and sideslip +/-0.523598776 rad, and recover useful regulation after the gust. The trim, guidance, control allocation and actuator dynamics methods are not prescribed.

Log four complete-run MATLAB Timeseries named flight_state, air_data, actuation, and force_moment. flight_state has 15 channels in this order: north, east, altitude (m); north, east, and down inertial velocity (m/s); true airspeed (m/s); angle of attack, sideslip, roll, pitch, and yaw (rad); and body p, q, and r (rad/s). air_data has 6 channels in this order: air density (kg/m^3), dynamic pressure (Pa), Mach number (1), and applied gust north, east, and down (m/s). actuation has 10 channels in this order: commanded thrust (N), commanded elevator, aileron, rudder, and leading-edge flap (rad), followed by the corresponding five actual actuator outputs in the same units. force_moment has 12 channels in this order: aerodynamic body force xyz (N), aerodynamic body moment xyz (N*m), total body force xyz including thrust and gravity (N), and total body moment xyz (N*m). All logs must come from one causal flight simulation and the reported actual actuators and loads must be the quantities used by the rigid-body plant.

Work directly in the required model file and keep the latest usable state saved at that path throughout the task.

Submission filename contract: create, edit, and save the final self-contained Simulink model as cand_XAERO03.slx in the assigned submission directory; keep the latest usable state at that exact path throughout the run.
